It is therefore ordered by the Public Utility Commission of Texas that new 16 TAC §25.194, relating to Large Load Interconnection Standards, is hereby adopted with changes to the text as proposed.

status.note: adopted by the order filed 18 September 2026 (the signature date on page 71 is illegible in the scan); effective 8 October 2026 per the Texas Register's acknowledgment (issue of 2 October 2026, TRD 202604027)

threshold_mw.value: 75 MW: a large load customer not energized by 8 October 2026 that seeks a new interconnection at a single site of 75 MW or more, an expansion reaching 75 MW for the first time, an expansion of a site over 75 MW by 75 MW or more, or co-location with a generation resource; at transmission or distribution voltage; for an expansion the rule applies to the added load

cites.quote: (b) Applicability. (1) This section applies to a large load customer that has not energized as of the effective date ofthis section and that seeks: (A) a new interconnection at a single site that is equal to or exceeds 75 megawatts (MW); (B) an expanded interconnection at a single site that equals or exceeds 75 MW for the first time; or (C) an expanded interconnection at a single site that exceeds 75 MW and is expanding by 75 MW or more; or (D) to co-locate with a generation resource.

(14) Large load customer -- An entity requesting a new or expanded interconnection where the customer's total expected non-coincident peak demand at a single site is equal to or exceeds 75 MW, whether at transmission voltage or distribution voltage.

min_demand.value: the SLLIA must include the customer's agreement to pay the large load minimum billing demand described in §25.193 for the period set there, and the utility may require additional security tied to it; the minimum billing demand itself is in §25.193, whose amendment (Project 58000) is pending and held by window A as a proposal

contract_term.value: no term printed in §25.194: an intermediate agreement before the study, then a commission-approved pro forma SLLIA (to be adopted in a future rulemaking) whose minimum billing obligation runs for the period set in §25.193

cites.quote: (17) Standard large load interconnection agreement (SLLIA) -- A commissionapproved pro forma agreement that is executed by a large load customer, the interconnecting DSP, and if different from the interconnecting DSP, the interconnecting TSP; and that, at a minimum, complies with this section.
The commission plans to adopt a SLLIA in a future rulemaking project.
acknowledgment and agreement that the large load customer will pay the large load minimum billing demand described in §25.193 ofthis title for the setperiod oftime described in §25.193.

collateral.value: intermediate agreement: $50,000 per MW of requested peak demand (or of the incremental increase), posted at execution; SLLIA: the greater of $50,000 per MW of contracted peak demand or the system upgrade costs allocated by the (batch zero) interconnection study, posted at SLLIA execution, plus possible additional security for the minimum billing demand; accepted forms: cash in a segregated interest-bearing account, a guaranty from a guarantor rated at least BBB- (S&P), Baa3 (Moody's) or BBB- (Fitch), or a letter of credit from a bank rated at least A-, A3 or A-; the $50,000 adjusted by CPI every five years from 2032; direct interconnection costs paid as non-refundable cash CIAC with no allowance

cites.quote: A large load customer must post financial security with the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP in the amount of $50,000 per MW of the requested peak demand for new interconnection requests or $50,000 per MW of the incremental increase in the peak demand for expanded interconnection requests.
A large load customer must post financial security with the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP in an amount that is the greater of: (I) $50,000 per MW ofthe contracted peak demand; or
the costs allocated to the large load customer for system upgrades as a result of a batch zero interconnection study or an interconnection study.
Financial security under this subsection must be posted at the time the SLLIA is executed.
(I) cash collateral to be held in a segregated, cash account bearing interest at a rate equal to at least the rate of the constant maturity one-month U.S. Treasury bill
guaranty, only if the guarantor has a U.S. or international credit rating of at least "BBB-" from Standard & Poor's, "Baa3" from Moody's Investor Service, or "BBB-" from Fitch.

a letter of credit issued by a major U.S. commercial bank, or a U.S. branch office of a major foreign commercial bank, with a U.S. or international credit rating of at least "A-" from Standard & Poor's, "A3" from Moody's Investor Service, or "A-" from Fitch.
Beginning in 2032, the commission will adjust the $50,000 value on January 1 every five years in accordance with this clause.

A large load customer must pay all direct interconnection costs through CIAC, with no standard or other allowance offered to offset the customer's CIAC payments. (i) CIAC must be paid in the form of a direct cash payment.
(v) CIAC is not refundable.

exit_fee.value: outstanding amounts owed are paid first (costs incurred, non-cancellable equipment, construction and services, and after a SLLIA the minimum billing demand for its set period); withdrawal before the study, or after a zero-MW allocation: full return of the rest; withdrawal after a partial allocation but before the SLLIA deadline: 20% of the security for the allocated capacity kept (50% for batch zero loads under Planning Guide 9.2.1.1(1)(f)); no SLLIA by the deadline: security forfeited; withdrawal of contracted demand after a SLLIA: 20% of the security for the withdrawn demand kept; energization schedule missed by 24 months: security drawn for amounts owed and 20% of the security for the non-utilized capacity kept; CIAC not refundable

study_timeline.value: $100,000 study fee due at execution of the intermediate agreement (ERCOT may add a flat fee); the TSP or DSP must contact ERCOT to start the study within 60 days after the intermediate agreement is executed and funded, and tell the customer within five working days; unused study fee returned within 60 days after the study ends

cites.quote: (i) A large load customer must pay a study fee of $100,000 to the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP for transmission studies performed by the interconnecting DSP, the interconnecting TSP, and ERCOT, as applicable.
(iv) The study fee is due not later than the date that the intermediate agreement is executed.

Not later than 60 days after an intennediate agreement is executed and funded under subsection (d) of this section, the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP must contact ERCOT to initiate an interconnection study, as prescribed by ERCOT protocols.

The interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP must notify the large load customer not later than five working days after the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP contacts ERCOT to initiate an interconnection study.
(vi) Any unused study amount of the study fee must be returned to the large load customer not later than 60 days after the conclusion of the interconnection study.

connection_timeline.value: SLLIA executed and funded within 60 days after ERCOT's study report allocating capacity, or the request is cancelled; if the customer fails by 24 months to meet a milestone of its phased energization schedule (the schedule as a whole), the TSP or DSP notifies ERCOT within 30 days and ERCOT may reallocate the capacity; security returned 20% at energization and the rest in 20% steps as the minimum billing demand milestones are met

cites.quote: Not later than 60 days after ERCOT issues a study report that allocates transmission capacity, the large load customer must execute and fund a SLLIA with the interconnecting DSP and, if different from the interconnecting DSP, the interconnecting TSP.

Not later than 30 days after a large load customer fails, by 24 months, to satisfy a milestone in its schedule for phased energization, as described in the SLLIA at the time of execution, the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP must notify ERCOT of the large load customer's non-utilized capacity.
The 24-month period applies to the energization schedule as a whole, and not for each energization milestone individually.

rows.erw_overlap: Not held. large_load_connection_rules/puct_project_58000_proposal.yaml is the separate tariff rulemaking (proposed amendments to 25.192 and 25.193 and new 25.252: 20-year agreement, 240 payments); it is still pending (the latest filing in Project 58000, item 70 of 1 October 2026, is comments on the minimum billing demand study), and §25.194 relies on its §25.193 minimum billing demand. ercot_planning_guide_section_9.yaml and ercot_large_load_batch_update_april_2026.yaml hold ERCOT's own Batch Zero clocks and threshold; §25.194(h) sets the PUCT's return and forfeiture terms for batch zero load, which those files do not hold.
rows.notes: The rule binds electric utilities, municipally owned utilities and electric cooperatives interconnecting large loads to the ERCOT system (subsection (a)); a municipally owned utility or cooperative may add its own requirements: 'Nothing in this section limits the authority of a municipally owned utility or an electric cooperative to impose electric service requirements for large load customers on their systems in addition to the standards adopted under this section' (page 25). Also in the rule, not entered as fields: required disclosures under both agreements (site control with a lease of at least five years, substantially similar requests elsewhere in Texas, water, backup generation, power supply, controllable load resource), audit and verification by ERCOT and commission staff with forfeiture and reallocation for false information (subsections (j), (k)), and the transition for customers that signed a §25.370(g) agreement (subsection (i)). A batch zero load with an interconnection agreement signed on or before 1 June 2025 pays direct interconnection costs under that agreement (subsection (h)(3)(B), page 65). The Texas Register's own pages were not read (sos.state.tx.us answered 403 on the October 9 issue; the adoption was submitted for the issue of 2 October 2026).

min_demand.value: billing demand is the highest of 50,000 kW, the Maximum Demand, or 80% of the highest measured summer (June to September) demand in the past 12 months; the Monthly Minimum Charge is the customer and demand charges plus fixed riders, facilities charges and tax

cites.quote: The Billing Demand (in kW) will be the highest of: A. 50,000 kW; or B. The Maximum Demand, adjusted by the Meter Voltage Adjustment, if applicable; or C. 80% of the highest measured demand established during the billing months of June through September in the twelve (12) month period ending with the current month.
The Monthly Minimum Charge is the Customer Charge plus applicable Demand Charge plus, Other Non-Consumption Fixed Amount Applicable Riders, Facilities Charges and Tax Adjustment.
